# What Agent Drive is

This page explains what Agent Drive stores, what the service can and cannot see, and the terms used in the rest of these docs. Read it first if you are new to Agent Drive.

## What it is

Agent Drive is encrypted file storage for AI agents. An agent saves files to a drive as it works. The agent's machine encrypts each file before upload, so the service stores only ciphertext. When a sandbox ends or the work moves to another machine or another agent platform, the files are still in the drive.

A person signs up, then approves each agent once in the browser. The agent keeps the drive key on its own machine.

## What the service can and cannot see

| The service can see                                | The service cannot see                 |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| File paths, sizes and timestamps                   | File contents                          |
| Tags and descriptions you attach to files          | Drive keys                             |
| Which agent, machine and user wrote each version   | The decryption key inside a share link |
| Activity metadata (which operations ran, and when) |                                        |

Do not put secrets in file names, paths, tags or descriptions. Put them inside file contents, which are encrypted.

One exception: if you set up the OpenRouter webhook for [trace capture](trace-capture.md), the server receives each trace over TLS and encrypts it to the drive's inbox key. It never holds the drive key.

If you lose the drive key and have no recovery file, nobody can open the files, including us. See [Back up and recover your drive key](backup-and-recovery.md) and the [Threat model](threat-model.md).

## Terms

| Term               | Meaning                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| console            | The signed-in web app at `/console`.                                                                                                                          |
| drive              | A storage space for files, with its own drive key.                                                                                                            |
| drive key          | The encryption key for one drive. It is created on the agent's machine and never sent to the service.                                                         |
| recovery file      | A JSON file that holds one drive key, downloaded from the console. It is the backup of that drive key.                                                        |
| credentials bundle | One line of text (`adcred1.…`) that holds an API key and drive keys, written by `agent-drive credentials export`. It also works as a backup of the drive key. |
| agent              | A named identity that does work in your account. Every file version records which agent wrote it.                                                             |
| API key            | The secret an agent uses to call the API. Each key belongs to one agent, is limited to chosen drives, and has scopes.                                         |
| scope              | A permission on an API key: `read`, `write`, `delete`, `share`, `manage` or `delegate`. See below.                                                            |
| write paths        | An optional list of folders (up to 16) a key may write under.                                                                                                 |
| version            | One saved state of a file. Overwrites and restores create new versions.                                                                                       |
| trace              | A captured record of an agent's model calls, stored encrypted under `/traces`.                                                                                |
| share link         | An expiring link that lets someone without an account download one file version.                                                                              |

Scopes:

- `read`: list, read, search and view versions.
- `write`: upload, move, copy and restore files.
- `delete`: move files to the trash.
- `share`: create, list and revoke share links.
- `manage`: account-wide administration, such as creating agents, drives and keys.
- `delegate`: let an agent add other agents to its drives. It is granted only when the person ticks the option on the approval page.

A normal agent approval grants `read`, `write`, `delete` and `share`. It never grants `manage`.

## Ways to use it

- [CLI](cli.md): the `agent-drive` command.
- [MCP server and tools](mcp-tools.md): run `agent-drive mcp` so an MCP client can call the tools.
- [Agent skills](skills.md): the `agent-drive` and `agent-drive-trace-archive` skills.
- [HTTP API](api.md): the API the CLI and console use.
- [The console](console.md): browse, preview, restore and share files, and manage agents, billing and your account.

## Where to start

Follow the [Quickstart](quickstart.md). Or give your agent this line and let it follow the setup guide:

```text
Set up Agent Drive: https://agentdrive.xyz/llms.txt
```

Agents can read `/llms.txt` for the docs index and the setup steps.

## Requirements

- Node 24 or newer.
- The npm package `@dennisonbertram/agent-drive`.
- The default API is `https://agentdrive.xyz/api`. Use `--api` or `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL` for a self-hosted installation.

Install the CLI globally:

```sh
npm install -g @dennisonbertram/agent-drive
```

Or run it without installing:

```sh
npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest login --name "<your agent name>"
```

With `npx`, put `npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest` in front of every command in these docs instead of `agent-drive`.

# Quickstart

This page walks you through connecting an agent to Agent Drive, backing up its credentials, and storing and sharing a first file. Run the steps in order as a checklist.

Alternative start: give your agent this line, and it follows the same steps from the setup guide.

```text
Set up Agent Drive: https://agentdrive.xyz/llms.txt
```

## 1. Sign up

Create your account at [/sign-up](https://agentdrive.xyz/sign-up).

## 2. Install the CLI

Agent Drive needs Node 24 or newer.

```sh
npm install -g @dennisonbertram/agent-drive
```

If global installs are not allowed, put this prefix in front of every command below instead of `agent-drive`:

```sh
npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest
```

## 3. Log in and approve

```sh
agent-drive login --name "<your agent name>"
```

The CLI prints a link and a code. Open the link while signed in, check that the code matches the one in the terminal, and click Approve. The command finishes by itself. You do not copy an API key.

For a self-hosted installation, pass its API URL:

```sh
agent-drive login --name "<your agent name>" --api https://<your-origin>/api
```

## 4. Back up the credentials

The drive key exists only on this machine. If the machine or sandbox is deleted, the files can never be opened again. Back up the credentials now. Offer these choices in this order and let the person pick one.

1Password (needs the `op` CLI, signed in). This counts as the backup at once:

```sh
agent-drive credentials export --to 1password
```

Clipboard (macOS and Windows). Paste the credentials into Apple Passwords or another password manager, then confirm:

```sh
agent-drive credentials export --to clipboard
agent-drive credentials confirm
```

The clipboard is cleared after 60 seconds if it still holds the credentials. Add `--keep-clipboard` to skip that.

A file on a path that survives the sandbox. The file has mode 600 and counts as the backup at once:

```sh
agent-drive credentials export --to <path outside the sandbox>
```

## 5. Check

```sh
agent-drive check
```

Setup is complete only when this prints `check ok`. It refuses to pass until step 4 is done. A read-only agent prints `check ok ... (read-only)` once the drive holds a file. On an empty drive it prints `check not verified`, so run it again after another agent writes a file.

## 6. Store, fetch and share a file

```sh
printf 'hello from an agent\n' > sample.txt
agent-drive put ./sample.txt /sample.txt
agent-drive get /sample.txt --output ./downloaded.txt
cmp ./sample.txt ./downloaded.txt
agent-drive share /sample.txt --expires-in 24h
```

`cmp` prints nothing when the files match. If you have more than one drive, add `--drive <drive id>` to each command.

The full share URL is a secret. Its fragment (the part after `#`) holds the file decryption key. Do not log it or post it anywhere you do not trust. See [Share links](sharing.md).

## 7. Optional: skill and MCP

Install the skill so the agent saves and recalls files without being asked:

```sh
agent-drive skill install
```

This writes into `~/.claude/skills` or `~/.codex/skills`, whichever of `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` exists. In a sandbox, CI or on a shared machine, use `agent-drive skill install --target <dir>`.

Add the MCP server to Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add agent-drive -- agent-drive mcp
```

Other MCP clients run the command `agent-drive` with the argument `mcp`. See [MCP server and tools](mcp-tools.md) and [Agent skills](skills.md).

## Next steps

- [Connect an agent](connect-an-agent.md): add more agents and limit what they can do.
- [Files, versions and sync](files-and-sync.md): work with files, versions and folders.
- [Using Agent Drive in sandboxes](sandboxes.md): keep a drive across sandboxes that are deleted.
- [The console](console.md): browse, restore and share files in the browser, and manage billing and your account.

# Connect an agent

This page helps you log in an agent, approve it in the browser, add more agents to the same drive, and limit what each agent can do. It also lists the common login errors and their fixes.

## How login works

`agent-drive login` uses a device flow. The CLI prints a link and a code. A person opens the link while signed in to Agent Drive, checks that the code matches the one in the terminal, and clicks Approve. The CLI finishes by itself. Nobody copies an API key.

The request expires after 10 minutes. If it expires, run `agent-drive login` again.

Default on Approve:

- Scopes `read`, `write`, `delete` and `share`. Never `manage`.
- A new drive named after the agent. The agent creates the drive key on its own machine. Agent Drive never sees it.

The approval page shows these defaults in a summary line. Click Details to see them as a list. Details also has a checkbox, "Let this agent add other agents to its drives", which adds the `delegate` scope. Tick it only for an agent that must hand its drive to other agents.

Login never prints an API key or a drive key. It prints the agent name, the usable drives, the scopes and the config file path.

## Log in

```sh
agent-drive login --name "<your agent name>"
```

Without `--name`, the agent is named `<machine name> agent`.

The CLI opens the link in a browser when stdout is a terminal and `CI` is not set. To print the link only:

```sh
agent-drive login --name "<your agent name>" --no-browser
```

For a self-hosted installation, add the API URL:

```sh
agent-drive login --name "<your agent name>" --api https://<your-origin>/api
```

To save an API key you already have, without the browser flow, pipe it in:

```sh
printf '%s' "<api key>" | agent-drive login --api https://agentdrive.xyz/api --token-stdin
```

This saves the API key only. It does not give the machine any drive key.

Environment variables:

- `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL` sets the API URL.
- `AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY` supplies an API key. If it is set, `login` saves that key instead of starting the browser flow.
- `AGENT_DRIVE_CONFIG` sets the config file path.

The CLI keeps its settings in `~/.config/agent-drive/config.json` (mode 600) unless `AGENT_DRIVE_CONFIG` says otherwise. The default API URL is `https://agentdrive.xyz/api`.

## Reconnect

Run `agent-drive login` again on the same machine, with the same `--name` and API origin. The CLI sends its saved API key as proof. If that key is still valid, the approval reconnects the agent to the drives it used before, and keeps its previous permissions. The drive keys already on the machine stay in place.

Login issues a new API key, so credential backups made earlier are out of date. The CLI says so and clears the backup records. Run `agent-drive credentials export` again (see [Back up and recover your drive key](backup-and-recovery.md)).

## Add another agent

Choose the handoff that fits.

| Situation                                                                                                     | Use                                |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| The new agent has a shell, a person is present, and an existing agent holds the `delegate` scope              | `grant`                            |
| The new agent has a shell, a person is present, and they have the drive's recovery file or credentials bundle | Recovery file on the approval page |
| The new agent is in a sandbox with no browser, and an existing agent holds `delegate`                         | `credentials issue`                |

### Grant from an agent that holds the drive

1. On the new agent's machine, run `agent-drive login --name "<new agent name>"`. It prints a code.
2. On the agent that holds the drive, run:

```sh
agent-drive grant <code> --write-path <folder>
```

Add `--read-only` for read only. Add `--drive <drive id>` if the machine holds more than one drive key. `--scope` (repeatable) sets the scopes explicitly.

The command seals the drive key to the new login and prints the approval URL. A person still clicks Approve on that page, which shows "Offered by" with the agent name, the drive and the permissions. Nothing secret is printed or sent in the clear.

The granting key needs the `delegate` scope. An agent cannot grant more than it holds, and cannot pass on `delegate`. If the granting key is limited to write paths, the new agent's write paths must be inside them.

### Use a recovery file on the approval page

1. On the new agent's machine, run `agent-drive login --name "<new agent name>"`.
2. Open the link, click Details, and choose "Use one of my drives instead (needs its recovery file)".
3. Pick the drive. Choose the recovery file, or paste the drive key or an `adcred1.` credentials bundle. Your browser seals the key to the new agent. Agent Drive never sees it.
4. Optional: tick Read only, or enter a folder to allow writes under.
5. Click Approve agent.

This option appears only on a new request, when your account already has a drive. A recovery file or credentials bundle is checked against the drive. A pasted key cannot be checked in the browser.

### Issue credentials for a sandbox

From an agent whose key has `delegate`:

```sh
agent-drive credentials issue --name "<new agent name>" --write-path <folder> --stdout
```

Send the output into the platform's secret store, then tell the person to set it as `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` there. Do not copy your own credentials into another agent's environment. To write to a file instead of stdout, use `--to <path>`.

If your key lacks `delegate`, ask the person to approve you again with "Let this agent add other agents to its drives" ticked. See [Using Agent Drive in sandboxes](sandboxes.md).

## Limit an agent

- Read only: use `--read-only` with `grant`, or tick Read only on the approval page.
- Scopes: `--scope read --scope write` with `grant`, `credentials issue` or `key create`. A key with `delegate` (used by `grant` and `credentials issue`) can hand out only `read`, `write`, `delete` and `share`, and only the ones it holds. It never grants `manage` or `delegate`. A key with `manage` (used by `key create`) can create keys with any scope.
- Write paths: `--write-path <folder>` limits writes to a folder. Repeat it for up to 16 folders. A folder starts with `/` and does not end with `/`, for example `/inbox/agent`.
- Revoke: in the console, open Agents and choose Revoke access, or open API keys and revoke one key. A revoked key stops working at its next request.

To create a scoped key by hand, you need a key with the `manage` scope:

```sh
agent-drive key create --agent <agent id> --drive <drive id> --label "<label>" --scope read --scope write --write-path /inbox
agent-drive key revoke <key id>
```

Without `--scope`, `key create` grants `read` and `write`. The API key is shown once; the service keeps only a hash.

## Check and troubleshoot

```sh
agent-drive whoami
agent-drive check
```

`whoami` prints the agent, its drives and scopes, and which drives have a key on this machine. `check` must print `check ok`.

| Message                                       | Fix                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| no usable drive key                           | Run `agent-drive login` again. The approval creates a drive for this agent.      |
| The API key lacks a scope                     | Run `agent-drive login` again. Do not run `agent-drive drive create`.            |
| The API key may only write under some folders | Not a login problem. Write under those folders.                                  |
| The approval link asks you to sign in         | Sign in first, then click Approve.                                               |
| The login code expired                        | Run `agent-drive login` again.                                                   |
| drive key not backed up                       | Run one of the `credentials export` commands in the [Quickstart](quickstart.md). |

Chat assistants that run in a vendor's cloud and have no shell on your machine are not supported. Encryption happens on the agent's own machine.

# The console

This page helps you use the console, the signed-in web app, to browse files, unlock a drive to open files, restore and share files, and manage agents, billing and your account. Sign in at [/sign-in](https://agentdrive.xyz/sign-in), then open `/console`.

## Sign in and drives

The side menu has these sections: Files, Agents, API keys, Usage, Trash, Billing & limits, and Activity & deletion.

Files lists the files in the selected drive. Use the drive menu at the top to switch drives or copy a drive ID. To create a drive in the browser, use New drive in that menu. The browser makes the drive key and offers a recovery file to download. Save it in a password manager, then click "I saved it". Nobody can recover the drive key for you.

Files has three views: Browse (folders), Recent (newest first) and Shared (share links).

While the console is locked it shows only metadata: paths, sizes, tags, authors and timestamps. It cannot show file contents until you unlock the drive.

## Unlock

The key chip near the top of Files shows the state: Key needed, Key loaded, Locked or Unlocked. A "Not backed up" note appears until a backup of the drive key is recorded.

Load the key in one of these ways:

- Recovery file: choose the recovery file for the drive. The file is named like `agent-drive-<id>.key.json`.
- Pasted key: open "Paste a key instead" and paste the drive key, or an `adcred1.` credentials bundle from `agent-drive credentials export`.
- Passphrase: set up passphrase unlock once, then a passphrase opens the drives you added to your account. A passphrase is at least 14 characters, or you can use one the browser generates. "Forgot or exposed passphrase?" resets it. A reset removes every drive from your account key but does not delete files; you add each drive again with its recovery file.

The key stays in memory in this browser tab. It is cleared when you reload the page or leave the Files page, or after 30 minutes without use. The key is not saved in browser storage.

If you have no recovery file, ask the agent that created the drive to run:

```sh
agent-drive credentials export
```

## Files

With the drive unlocked you can:

- Preview a file. Text and images show in a dialog. Large files, binary files and unknown types show a message instead. Use Download for those.
- Download a file. It is decrypted in the browser.
- Open Versions from the row menu. Each version shows its time, size and author. "Restore this version" makes an older version the current one by creating a new version. Existing history stays.
- Trash a file from the row menu.

Version and trash behavior:

- Overwriting a file or restoring an older version creates a new version.
- Restoring a file's current version from Trash only brings it back. It creates no new version.
- Trash does not free storage. All versions count toward storage, including files in Trash.

The Trash section lists deleted files with a Restore button.

## Shares

Choose Share from a file's row menu. Pick how long the link lasts (1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days) and click Copy link. The link is a secret. It can be copied only when it is created, and anyone who has it can download that version of the file. Later changes are not included.

The dialog lists the links for the file with their state: Active, Expired, Revoked, or Unavailable (file in Trash). Use Revoke on an active link to stop it. The Shared view lists links for the whole drive. See [Share links](sharing.md).

## Traces

On Files, the Traces button opens the `/traces` folder in the Recent view. Capture… opens the setup dialog:

- Local agents: shows the install command and the `agent-drive capture --drive <drive id> -- claude` command. See [Capture traces](trace-capture.md).
- OpenRouter webhook: Add webhook shows a webhook URL and a headers JSON once. Copy both into an OpenRouter Webhook destination, and leave Privacy Mode off for it, or traces will contain no prompts or replies. Replace makes a new token. Revoke webhook stops it.

Setting up the webhook needs the drive key loaded, so the console may ask you to unlock the drive first.

## Agents and API keys

Agents lists the agents in your account. The Connect an agent panel shows the line to give an agent and MCP setup snippets. Create an agent makes an identity without a login. Revoke access on an agent revokes all of its API keys.

API keys lists keys with their state. Create API key asks for a label, an agent, the allowed drives and the permissions. Read and write are ticked by default. The secret is shown once; copy it and tick "I saved my API key securely". Revoke a key when you no longer need it. Revoked keys stop working at their next request. See [Connect an agent](connect-an-agent.md).

## Billing

[/console/billing](https://agentdrive.xyz/console/billing) (Billing & limits) shows:

- Plan allowances, retained storage and API operations for the current month.
- Spending controls: a monthly write cap in USD, an alert threshold and an alert email. A write cap stops new writes once estimated spend reaches it. It does not stop reads and is not a guaranteed invoice limit. A cap of zero blocks new writes immediately.
- Usage by agent, with a CSV download for a chosen month.
- Invoices & payment details, when your account has a billing customer.

For plans and prices see [/pricing](https://agentdrive.xyz/pricing). Paid checkout may be disabled on a deployment; the billing page shows what is available.

## Settings

[/console/settings](https://agentdrive.xyz/console/settings) (Activity & deletion) shows:

- Activity: the audit log for your account, most recent first. It holds metadata only, never file contents or credentials.
- Passphrase unlock status, with a link to manage it in Files.
- Delete your data: delete one drive (type its exact name) or delete your account (type `DELETE MY ACCOUNT`).
- Deletion requests: the status of each request.

Deletion cannot be undone. It removes retained versions, trash, share links and upload metadata. When a request is accepted, new access is disabled and a background purge is queued. The purge starts after the upload grace period (at least ten minutes). Storage or billing failures delay completion and are retried. Already-issued links may work until they expire. Accepting the request does not prove that every byte is erased yet; check Deletion requests for completion. Account deletion also closes billing and removes your sign-in identity.

# Files, versions and sync

This page shows how to store, read, search, version and restore files in a drive, and how to upload whole folders with `sync` and `backup`. Every example uses the `agent-drive` command. If you have not installed it, see the [CLI reference](cli.md), or put `npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest` in front of each command.

The MCP server offers the same operations under different tool names (for example `ls` is `list`). The mapping table is in [MCP server and tools](mcp-tools.md).

## Paths and drives

A path is a canonical absolute path such as `/work/report/notes.md`. It must start with `/`, must not end with `/`, and must not contain `//`, `\`, `.` or `..` parts. A path is at most 1024 characters.

Paths, tags and descriptions are stored in plain text on the service. File contents are encrypted on your machine before upload. Never put secrets in a path, tag or description.

Every file command takes `--drive ID`. You can leave it out when exactly one drive key is saved for the current API origin. If there are none or several, the command fails and lists the configured drive IDs:

```text
A --drive ID is required. Configured drives for this API: <drive id 1>, <drive id 2>.
```

Pass `--drive <drive id>` in that case. The examples below omit it.

## Write a file

`put` encrypts a local file and uploads it. By default it only creates: it fails if the path already exists.

```sh
agent-drive put ./notes.md /work/report/notes.md --tag report --description "Draft notes"
```

`--tag` can be repeated. `--description` and `--user ID` are optional. The command prints the new version as JSON, including its `id`.

To replace a file, choose one of two flags. They cannot be combined.

```sh
# Replace without checking. The old content stays as an earlier version.
agent-drive put ./notes.md /work/report/notes.md --overwrite

# Replace only if the file is still at the version you read.
agent-drive put ./notes.md /work/report/notes.md --if-version <version id>
```

Use `--if-version` whenever another agent may write the same file. Do not use `--overwrite` to win a race.

### When a write conflicts

A conditional write that loses returns a conflict. The CLI prints a message and a hint, and exits with code 1. The state tells you why.

| State     | Meaning                                                   | What the CLI prints                                                                             | What to do                                                                                         |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `exists`  | You wrote create-only and the file already exists.        | `Current version: ID. Read the file again, merge your change, then retry with --if-version ID.` | Read the file, merge your change, then retry with `--if-version ID`.                               |
| `changed` | The file moved past the version you passed.               | The same line as `exists`.                                                                      | Same as `exists`.                                                                                  |
| `trashed` | The file is in the trash.                                 | `The file is in the trash: restore it with "restore <path>" or write with --overwrite.`         | Run `restore PATH`, or write with `--overwrite`. A conditional write never revives a trashed file. |
| `absent`  | You passed `--if-version` but no file exists at the path. | `There is no file at this path now; write it without --if-version.`                             | Run `put` without `--if-version`.                                                                  |

Example recovery after `changed`:

```sh
agent-drive get /work/report/notes.md --output ./notes.latest.md
# Merge your change into ./notes.latest.md, then:
agent-drive put ./notes.latest.md /work/report/notes.md --if-version <current version id>
```

## Read a file

```sh
agent-drive get /work/report/notes.md
```

Without `--output`, `get` prints the file only when it is valid UTF-8 text of at most 1 MiB with no binary control bytes (tabs and line breaks are fine). Otherwise it fails with `Binary or large output requires --output.`

```sh
agent-drive get /work/report/notes.md --output ./notes.md
agent-drive get /work/report/notes.md --version <version id> --output ./notes.old.md
```

With `--output`, the file is written (mode `0600`) only after the content has been decrypted and authenticated. The command then prints the version metadata. It never prints the download URL or the wrapped file key.

## List and find

```sh
agent-drive ls --prefix /work
agent-drive ls --folder /work
agent-drive ls --sort modified --limit 20
agent-drive ls --prefix /work --agent <agent id> --machine <machine name> --tag report
```

| Flag                                                     | Effect                                                                                                                                                                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--prefix PATH`                                          | Lists every file whose path starts with `PATH`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `--folder PATH`                                          | Lists the immediate children of `PATH`: file rows and folder rows. A folder row has `kind`, `path`, `items`, `ciphertext_size` and `created_at`. Cannot be combined with `--prefix`. |
| `--sort path\|modified`                                  | `path` is the default. `modified` lists the newest first.                                                                                                                            |
| `--agent ID`, `--machine NAME`, `--user ID`, `--tag TAG` | Filter by author agent, machine, user or tag. Only the first `--tag` is used.                                                                                                        |
| `--limit N`, `--cursor C`                                | Page through results. Each page returns `nextCursor`; pass it back as `--cursor` for the next page.                                                                                  |

`search` matches paths and attribution metadata, not file contents, because contents are encrypted.

```sh
agent-drive search --query report --tag report
```

`recent` lists file operations (`put`, `copy`, `restore`, `move`, `delete`) in the order they were committed. Each event names the path, the version and the author agent.

```sh
agent-drive recent --since 2026-11-09T00:00:00Z
agent-drive recent --cursor <latestCursor from the last call>
agent-drive recent --cursor <latestCursor from the last call> --wait 60
```

- Keep the `latestCursor` from one response and pass it as `--cursor` to see only newer events. With a cursor, `--since` is ignored.
- `--wait SECONDS` (1 to 300) polls every 2 seconds and returns when the next event arrives or the time ends. Each poll counts as one metered operation, so use it only while you are actually waiting for another agent.
- Store the cursor in your own session state, not in the drive.

## Move, copy, delete

```sh
agent-drive mv /work/report/notes.md /outputs/report-notes.md
agent-drive cp /work/report/notes.md /outputs/report-copy.md
agent-drive cp /work/report/notes.md /outputs/report-old.md --version <version id>
agent-drive rm /outputs/report-copy.md
```

- `mv` renames a file.
- `cp` copies the current version, or the version you pass with `--version`, to a new path.
- `rm` moves the file to the trash. `restore` brings it back.

Ask the user before deleting or overwriting anything you did not create.

## Versions and restore

Every write creates a new version. List them with:

```sh
agent-drive versions /work/report/notes.md
```

Each version shows its id, path, size, author and timestamps.

`restore` has two behaviors:

```sh
# Undelete a trashed file. Creates no new version.
agent-drive restore /outputs/report-copy.md

# Make an older version the current one. Creates a new version.
agent-drive restore /work/report/notes.md --version <older version id>
```

- Without `--version`, or with the file's current version, `restore` undeletes a trashed file and returns the existing version. On a live file it does nothing.
- With any other version, `restore` copies that version as a new current version.

## Sync a folder

`sync` uploads a local folder to a drive prefix. It is upload-only. It does not download, and it is not a mirror.

```sh
agent-drive sync ./project --prefix /work/project
```

Output is JSON with `uploaded`, `skipped`, `conflicts`, `accountId` and `manifestPath`.

Rules:

- The default prefix is `/`.
- Symlinks are skipped. The local root must be a real directory, not a symlink.
- It never deletes remote files.
- Unchanged files are skipped, using a SHA-256 hash and the version id recorded in a private manifest.
- Manifests live in `<config path>.state` (by default `~/.config/agent-drive/config.json.state`), outside the uploaded folder. The directory must be private to your user; an unsafe directory is rejected.
- A corrupt manifest stops the sync with an error. It does not reset the history.
- If a remote file changed since your last sync, the command stops with `Remote conflict for <path>; refusing to overwrite.` and exits with code 1. Files uploaded before that point stay uploaded.

### First adoption of a non-empty prefix

If the prefix already holds files that this machine never synced, sync stops with `Remote file <path> has no local sync history; use --overwrite-existing to replace it.` Use the flag once, on purpose:

```sh
agent-drive sync ./project --prefix /work/project --overwrite-existing
```

The overwrite still checks the current remote version. After the first run, a file with manifest history conflicts whenever its remote version changed.

## Back up a folder

`backup` uploads every regular file under a folder, with overwrite, so earlier versions are kept.

```sh
agent-drive backup ./workdir
agent-drive backup ./workdir --prefix /backups/my-project
agent-drive backup ./workdir --dry-run
```

- The default prefix is `/backups/<machine>`. The machine name is `AGENT_DRIVE_MACHINE` if set, otherwise the host name.
- `--prefix` must be an absolute path.
- Unchanged files are skipped (SHA-256 manifest in `<config path>.state`).
- Symlinks are skipped. The CLI config file, its lock and state, and the `--key-file` file are never uploaded.
- A file over 5 GiB fails. One failing file does not stop the rest; each failure prints `failed <path>: <reason>` on stderr.
- `--dry-run` prints `would upload <remote path>` for each file that would be sent and uploads nothing.

The last line on stdout is:

```text
backup uploaded=12 unchanged=40 failed=0
```

The command exits with code 1 if `failed` is above 0. Run `backup` before a sandbox or container ends.

The two commands differ in one way. `backup` always overwrites and never reports conflicts, so use it for a directory that only one agent writes. `sync` refuses to overwrite files that changed on the remote since your last run.

## Working with several agents on one drive

- Write shared files with `--if-version <id>` (MCP `ifVersionId`) after reading them. Only conditional writes detect conflicts.
- On a conflict, read the current version, merge, and retry with the new id. See the table above.
- To see what other agents changed, call `recent` and keep the `latestCursor`. Pass it back next time. Use `--wait` only while you are waiting.
- Each event names the author agent. Set `AGENT_DRIVE_MACHINE` to a clear name on each machine so that events and `ls --machine` filters tell machines apart.
- Give each agent its own folder, for example `/work/<agent name>` or `/inbox/<agent name>`. A key can be limited to specific write paths; see [Connect an agent](connect-an-agent.md).
- Tags, descriptions, paths and author names are plain text on the service. Put secrets only inside file contents.
- The [agent skill](skills.md) tells agents to follow these rules without being asked.

# Share links

This page shows how to share one file from a drive with a link that expires, and how to list and revoke links. The recipient needs no account.

## What a share link is

A share link is a secret. Anyone who holds the full URL can read the file until the link expires or you revoke it.

The URL has this shape:

```text
https://agentdrive.xyz/s/<share id>#k=<file decryption key>
```

The part after `#` is the URL fragment. It carries the key that decrypts this one file. Browsers do not send the fragment to servers, so the service never receives the key and cannot read the file. If the fragment is lost, nobody can open the file from that link, including you.

Treat the whole URL as a password. Do not share a file that contains secrets.

## Create a link

CLI:

```sh
agent-drive share /outputs/report.pdf --expires-in 24h
```

- `PATH` is the file to share.
- `--expires-in` takes a number and a unit: `m`, `h` or `d`, for example `30m`, `24h` or `7d`. The CLI accepts 2 minutes to 30 days. If you leave it out, the service uses 7 days.
- `--version ID` shares a specific version instead of the current one. The link points to one version; later writes to the path do not change what it shows.

The command prints JSON with `id`, `path`, `versionId`, `expiresAt` and `url`. Send `url` to the recipient. Your API key needs the `share` scope on the drive.

MCP: call the `share` tool with `path`, and optionally `driveId`, `versionId` and `expiresAt` (an ISO 8601 timestamp). It returns the same fields. See [MCP server and tools](mcp-tools.md).

Console: open the file, choose Share, pick an expiry (1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days; 7 days is the default) and copy the link. See [The console](console.md).

## List and revoke

```sh
agent-drive share list
agent-drive share revoke <share id>
```

`share list` shows each link's `id`, `path`, `versionId`, `expiresAt`, `revokedAt`, `createdAt` and `status`. The status is one of:

| Status        | Meaning                        |
| ------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `active`      | The link works.                |
| `expired`     | The expiry time has passed.    |
| `revoked`     | The owner turned the link off. |
| `unavailable` | The file is in the trash.      |

The list does not include the URL or key, so it cannot rebuild a lost link. Create a new link instead. Add `--limit N` and `--cursor C` to page through a long list. `share revoke` prints the share id and the revocation time.

## What the recipient sees

The recipient opens the URL in a browser. The page at `/s/<share id>`:

1. Reads the key from the URL fragment.
2. Asks the service for the file name, size and expiry. When the recipient downloads, the service returns a short-lived download URL for the encrypted file.
3. Downloads the encrypted bytes and decrypts them in the browser.
4. Saves the decrypted file under its original file name.

If something is wrong, the page says so. The cases are: a missing key, a link that was not found, a revoked link, an expired link, a file that is no longer available, and a key that does not match the file. A link with less than one second left cannot start a download.

## Limits and risks

- The service enforces expiry. After it, the page shows "Share link expired".
- Revoking a link stops new downloads. It cannot take back a copy someone already downloaded, or a key someone already saved.
- Anyone with the complete URL can open the file. The service does not ask who they are.
- Moving a file to the trash makes its links `unavailable`. Whether restoring the file makes the links work again is TBD.
- Whether downloads through a share link count toward your plan's operation or egress limits is TBD; see [Errors and limits](errors.md).
- The service sees the file name, the size and who created the link. It does not see the contents. See the [Threat model](threat-model.md) and [Encryption format](crypto.md).

# Using Agent Drive in sandboxes

This page helps you keep an agent connected to its drive when it runs in disposable sandboxes, containers or CI jobs. You store the agent's credentials bundle once in a secret store, then give it to every new sandbox as `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS`.

## The problem

The drive key exists only on the machine where the agent logged in, in `~/.config/agent-drive/config.json`. If the sandbox is deleted, the key is gone and the files in the drive can never be opened again. A new sandbox also has no API key, so it would need a human to approve a new login.

The fix is a credentials bundle: one line of text (starting with `adcred1.`) that holds the agent's API key and drive key. Keep it in a secret store and set it as `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` in each sandbox.

## Set up once

Run this on the machine where the agent already logged in (see [Quickstart](quickstart.md)). Replace `<secret store command>` with a command that reads the bundle from stdin and saves it, for example a 1Password or cloud secret manager CLI.

```sh
set -o pipefail
agent-drive credentials export --stdout | <secret store command> && agent-drive credentials confirm
```

`--stdout` prints the bundle only when stdout is not a terminal, so you must pipe it. `set -o pipefail` makes the pipeline fail if the secret store command fails, so `confirm` runs only after the bundle was stored. `credentials confirm` records the backup. Without it, `agent-drive check` fails with "drive key not backed up".

Then, in your sandbox or CI platform, create a secret named `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` whose value is the bundle from the secret store.

Do not use a CI secret as the backup itself. Keep the bundle in a password manager or secret store you can read back, and copy it into CI from there. Other backup targets (`--to 1password`, `--to clipboard`, `--to PATH`) are in [Back up and recover your drive key](backup-and-recovery.md).

Never print the bundle in a chat, a log, or a file inside a drive.

## What each new sandbox does

When `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` is set, the CLI and the MCP server read it at startup:

- The bundle is merged in memory. It is never written to disk.
- Saved values win over the bundle. The explicit variables `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL`, `AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY` and `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>` also win over it. If the sandbox has no config file and none of those variables, the bundle supplies everything.
- The bundle's drives count as backed up (method `env`), so `agent-drive check` can pass. This applies only when the effective API key is the bundle's key and the API origin matches the origin the bundle recorded for the drive key. The CLI reports the backup to the service once per process; a failure to report is only a warning.

Check the result:

```sh
agent-drive whoami
agent-drive check
```

`check` must print `check ok`. If your agent is read-only, see [Common failures](#common-failures).

## One bundle per agent

Each agent that runs in a sandbox should have its own API key. Do not copy your own bundle into another agent's environment.

If your key has the `delegate` scope (check with `agent-drive whoami`), issue a separate bundle for the new agent. Replace the placeholders.

```sh
set -o pipefail
agent-drive credentials issue --name "<new agent name>" --write-path /work/<new agent name> --stdout | <secret store command>
```

The command creates a new agent with its own API key and prints one `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS=adcred1.…` line. The line holds only that key and the chosen drive's key. Your own API key and config are not included and not changed. Options:

| Option                | Meaning                                                                                            |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--name NAME`         | Required. The new agent's name. A name that already exists returns 409; pick another.              |
| `--drive ID`          | The drive to share. Defaults to the only drive key saved for the current API.                      |
| `--scope S`           | Repeat for each scope. Defaults to `read` and `write`. Must be within your own scopes.             |
| `--write-path P`      | Repeat to limit writes to folders.                                                                 |
| `--label L`           | Label for the new API key.                                                                         |
| `--to PATH [--force]` | Write the line to a mode 600 file instead of `--stdout`. Pass exactly one of `--to` or `--stdout`. |

Tell the human to set the stored value as `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` in the new sandbox. The line printed by `issue` starts with `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS=`; the value is the part after `=`.

If your key lacks `delegate`, ask the human to approve you again with "Let this agent add other agents" ticked on the approval page.

To remove one issued agent, revoke its API key in the [console](console.md) under Agents. Revoking it does not affect you or other agents.

## No global installs

If the sandbox does not allow global installs, prefix every command with `npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest`:

```sh
npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest whoami
npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest check
```

To install the agent skill in a sandbox, CI job or shared machine, give it a directory instead of using your home folder:

```sh
agent-drive skill install --target ./skills/agent-drive
```

See [Agent skills](skills.md).

## Environment variables

| Variable                     | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS`    | The credentials bundle (`adcred1.…`). Merged in memory, never written to disk.                                                                                                                    |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_CONFIG`         | Path of the config file. Default `~/.config/agent-drive/config.json`.                                                                                                                             |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL`        | API URL. Default `https://agentdrive.xyz/api`. Overrides the saved and bundle values.                                                                                                             |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY`        | API key. Overrides the saved and bundle values.                                                                                                                                                   |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_MACHINE`        | Machine name recorded with uploads. Default is the host name. Set a stable value in sandboxes.                                                                                                    |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>` | The drive key for one drive. Take the drive ID, make it uppercase, and replace each character that is not a letter or digit with `_`. Example: drive `3f2a-91` becomes `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_3F2A_91`. |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY`            | A drive key used for any drive that has no `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>`.                                                                                                                          |

Drive-key precedence is `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>`, then `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY`, then `--key-file` (CLI only), then the saved or bundle key. A key supplied through `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY*` or `--key-file` is outside the config and does not need a backup record for `check`.

## Common failures

- The sandbox cannot reach `https://agentdrive.xyz` (network blocked). Stop and tell the human. Do not try to work around it.
- `no usable drive key`: run `agent-drive whoami` and read `localDriveKeys`. A drive key counts only for the API origin it was saved for, so check that `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL` matches the bundle's origin. If it still fails, run `agent-drive login` again.
- `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS is not a valid credentials bundle.`: the value was truncated or has extra characters. Copy the bundle again. Do not paste the `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS=` prefix into the value.
- `drive key not backed up`: run `agent-drive credentials confirm` after the bundle is stored, or set `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` so the bundle counts as the backup.
- `check ok ... (read-only)` or `check not verified`: a read-only key cannot write the check file, so `check` decrypts an existing file instead. On an empty drive it prints `check not verified` and exits 1. Run it again after another agent writes a file. Do not report setup as complete until it prints `check ok`.
- MCP tools fail with "MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never" under `codex exec`: see [Codex approval](mcp-tools.md#codex-approval) in the MCP page.

# Back up and recover your drive key

This page shows how to back up an agent's credentials, check that the backup is recorded, and open your files again on a new machine or in the console. Do the backup right after the first login. A lost drive key cannot be recovered by Agent Drive, and without it nobody can decrypt the files in that drive.

For what each key is and what losing it means, see [Keys and recovery](keys-and-recovery.md).

## What you are backing up

The drive key exists only in the CLI config file (`~/.config/agent-drive/config.json`, or the path in `AGENT_DRIVE_CONFIG`). Agent Drive never receives it. If that file is lost, the files in the drive cannot be opened, and Agent Drive cannot restore the key for you.

`agent-drive credentials export` writes a credentials bundle: the text `adcred1.` followed by base64url of JSON. The bundle holds the API key and every drive key saved on this machine. Treat it as a secret. It is the only secret the CLI ever prints.

## Back up

Run one of these commands. Offer the targets to the person in this order: 1Password, clipboard, file.

### 1Password

```sh
agent-drive credentials export --to 1password
```

Use `--vault NAME` to choose a vault. `--to op` is an alias.

The CLI runs `op whoami`, then creates an item titled `Agent Drive – <drive ids>` with the bundle in a concealed field labelled `credentials`. The bundle goes to `op` on standard input. It is never in the command arguments and never written to disk.

On success the backup is recorded and `agent-drive check` can pass. Failure behavior:

- If the 1Password CLI (`op`) is not installed, the command exits non-zero and says so. Nothing is exported or recorded.
- If `op` is installed but not signed in, the command exits non-zero and tells you to sign in and check that `op whoami` succeeds. Nothing is recorded.
- If `op item create` fails, the command exits non-zero and records nothing.

### Clipboard

```sh
agent-drive credentials export --to clipboard
```

Paste the bundle into Apple Passwords or another password manager. Then record the backup:

```sh
agent-drive credentials confirm
```

The export alone records nothing. The CLI waits 60 seconds, then clears the clipboard only if it still holds the bundle. Add `--keep-clipboard` to skip the clear. If the clear fails, the CLI prints `Could not clear the clipboard; clear it yourself.`

The clipboard target works on macOS and Windows only. On Linux and WSL the command exits non-zero and suggests `--to 1password` or a file.

### File

```sh
agent-drive credentials export --to /path/outside/the/sandbox/agent-drive-credentials.txt
```

Choose a path that survives the machine or sandbox. The CLI writes the file with mode `0600` and records the backup at once. If the path already exists, the command fails with `<path> already exists; pass --force to overwrite it.` Add `--force` to replace it. A symlink destination is refused.

A file named `1password`, `op` or `clipboard` is read as a target name, not a path. Use `./clipboard` for such a file.

### Standard output

```sh
set -o pipefail
agent-drive credentials export --stdout | <your secret store command> && agent-drive credentials confirm
```

`--stdout` prints only when standard output is not a terminal. If it is a terminal, the command refuses and tells you to pipe it. A `--stdout` export records nothing, so run `credentials confirm` after the secret store has saved the bundle. `set -o pipefail` makes a failed store stop `confirm`.

### Other failures

- `There is no API key to back up. Run agent-drive login first.` Log in, then export again.
- `There are no drive keys on this machine to back up.` This machine has no drive key to save.

After a file, 1Password or `confirm` backup, the CLI also tells the service that a backup happened, with the method (`file` or `stdout`) and never the key. If that report fails, the CLI prints a warning and the local record still counts. The console then shows the drive as backed up.

## Check backup status

```sh
agent-drive credentials status
```

The output is JSON. Each drive key on this machine is listed with `backedUp`, and when backed up, `at` and `method`:

```json
{ "drives": { "<drive id>": { "backedUp": true, "at": "<ISO time>", "method": "file" } } }
```

The method is `file` for a file export or a `--from` import, `stdout` for 1Password, `credentials confirm` and imports from standard input, and `env` for a key that came from `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS`.

`agent-drive whoami` also prints `keyBackup`, a map from drive ID to the same record, or `null` for a drive with no backup.

`agent-drive check` refuses to pass until every usable drive key is backed up. It fails with `drive key not backed up: <drive ids>` and the backup commands above. A key supplied through `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>`, `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY` or `--key-file` is already outside the config file, so it is exempt.

## Restore on a new machine

1. Install the CLI. It needs Node 24 or newer.

   ```sh
   npm install -g @dennisonbertram/agent-drive
   ```

   To run without installing, prefix every command with `npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest`.

2. Import the bundle. From a file:

   ```sh
   agent-drive credentials import --from /path/to/agent-drive-credentials.txt
   ```

   Or from standard input, for example after copying the bundle out of a password manager (macOS):

   ```sh
   pbpaste | agent-drive credentials import
   ```

   The command merges the API URL, API key and drive keys into the config and marks those drives as backed up. It prints `imported <N> drive key(s) into <config path>`. A text that is not a valid bundle fails with `Not a valid Agent Drive credentials bundle.`

3. Check that the drive key opens the files.

   ```sh
   agent-drive check
   ```

   `check` must print `check ok`. If the key cannot decrypt existing files, it fails with `This drive key cannot decrypt existing files.`

For a sandbox that is deleted and recreated, you can skip the import. Set `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS` as a secret on the platform, holding the bundle. The CLI merges it in memory at startup, never writes it to disk, and counts its drives as backed up. The saved config and explicit `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL`, `AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY` and `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>` variables win over the bundle. See [Using Agent Drive in sandboxes](sandboxes.md).

### If the bundle holds a replaced API key

A bundle holds the API key that was current when you exported it. If a later `agent-drive login` replaced that key, the old key is revoked. The drive key in the old bundle still decrypts the files, but the API key does not work.

To give a new agent access to the old drive, run `agent-drive login` on it. On the approval page, open Details and choose "Use one of my drives instead", then load the recovery file or the bundle. The browser seals the drive key to the new agent. See [Connect an agent](connect-an-agent.md).

## Open files in the console

The console shows file names and metadata without any key. To decrypt and download a file in the browser, it needs the drive key. You have two ways to give it one:

- **Recovery file.** Choose "Load key" in the key menu, then "Choose recovery file" (or drop the file on the box). The recovery file is JSON named `agent-drive-<drive id>.key.json` with the fields `format` (`agent-drive-key-v1`), `driveId` and `key`. It must be under 16,384 bytes and its `driveId` must match the drive. Otherwise the console says `That recovery file is not for this drive.` or `That is not a recovery file.`
- **Pasted key or bundle.** Open "Paste a key instead" and paste the drive key or an `adcred1.` bundle. From a bundle the console takes the key for the selected drive only.

The key stays in that browser tab. It is cleared when you reload the page or after 30 minutes without use. It is not sent to the service and not saved in browser storage.

If you have no recovery file, ask the agent that created the drive to run `agent-drive credentials export`, then choose or paste what it gives you.

If you set up a passphrase in the console, you can unlock your drives with it instead. A passphrase slot is not a backup of the drive key. See [Keys and recovery](keys-and-recovery.md).

### Download a recovery file

When a drive key is loaded in the tab, choose "Download recovery file" in the key menu. The console also offers the file when it creates a drive. The file holds the key in plaintext, so store it in a password manager or another secure place. After the file saves, choose "I saved it". The console then records the backup with method `file`. The key is not sent.

## Back up folders (not keys)

Key backup is separate from file backup. To upload a working directory to the drive before a sandbox ends, use `agent-drive backup`. See [Files, versions and sync](files-and-sync.md).

## A login that replaces the API key

When `agent-drive login` saves a different API key, the CLI clears all local backup records. The old bundle holds the revoked key, so it no longer counts as a backup. The CLI prints:

```text
The API key changed, so earlier credential backups are out of date. Run `agent-drive credentials export` again.
```

`agent-drive check` then fails with `drive key not backed up` until you export again. The backup date that the console shows is stored by the service. Login does not clear it, so the console keeps showing the last reported backup until you export again.

## If the key is lost

- **Cannot be done:** Agent Drive cannot recover, reset or regenerate a drive key. The service never has it. The files stay encrypted and nothing in the service can open them.
- **Still possible:** if any one of these exists, you can restore access: a credentials bundle, a recovery file, the config file on any machine, a key in `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY*`, or a browser tab that has the key loaded. In the console, a loaded tab can download the recovery file.
- **Passphrase unlock:** if you set up a passphrase, the console can open drives that you added to your account. Resetting the passphrase removes every drive from the account and asks for each recovery file again. Files are not deleted.
- **No backup at all:** the file contents cannot be read. Paths, sizes, tags and version history remain visible in the console. Whether Agent Drive support can do anything else in this case: TBD, no support process is documented in the repository.

# Capture traces

This page shows how to save an agent's model traffic as encrypted traces, either by running the agent through `agent-drive capture` or by sending OpenRouter traces to a webhook, and how to archive old trace files from disk. Use it when you want a searchable, encrypted record of what an agent sent to and received from a model.

## What a trace is and where it is stored

A trace is a JSON file that records one model API exchange: the request and the response. It is stored in your drive like any other file, encrypted before upload.

- **CLI capture path:** `/traces/<agent>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS.mmm>Z_<model>_<id>.json`. `<id>` is 6 random hex characters.
- **OpenRouter webhook path:** `/traces/openrouter/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<HHMMSS.mmm>Z_<model>_<hash>.json`, where `<hash>` is the first 32 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the request body. If the payload has no usable span start time, the date folder is `undated` and the file is `/traces/openrouter/undated/<model>_<hash>.json`.
- **Tags:** `trace`, `agent:<agent>` and `model:<model>`. The model name is changed so that it holds only letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, and is cut to 50 characters. An unknown model is `unknown`.

The path and tags are plaintext metadata that the service can see. File contents are encrypted. See [Threat model](threat-model.md).

## Capture with the CLI

```sh
agent-drive capture [--drive ID] [--agent NAME] -- COMMAND [ARGS...]
```

For example:

```sh
agent-drive capture --drive <drive id> -- claude
agent-drive capture --drive <drive id> --agent my-agent -- codex
```

Everything after `--` belongs to COMMAND. Only the flags before `--` are read by `capture`.

What happens:

1. The CLI starts a proxy on `127.0.0.1` on a random port.
2. It starts COMMAND with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/anthropic` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openai` in the environment of that child process only. Your shell, shell profile, Claude settings and `~/.codex/config.toml` are not changed.
3. The proxy forwards each request unchanged to `api.anthropic.com` or `api.openai.com` and streams the response back as it arrives.
4. For each exchange it builds a redacted copy, encrypts it with the drive key, and queues it for upload.
5. When COMMAND exits, the CLI exits with the same exit code.

`--drive` can be left out when there is only one drive key saved for the current API. `--agent` defaults to the command's base name, in lowercase. It must be 1 to 40 characters: lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `_` or `-`, starting with a letter or digit.

For a command named `codex`, the CLI adds these arguments before yours, because Codex needs a provider entry and not only an environment variable:

```text
-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.name="Agent Drive capture"
-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.base_url="http://127.0.0.1:<port>/openai/v1"
-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.env_key="OPENAI_API_KEY"
-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.wire_api="responses"
-c model_providers.agent_drive_capture.supports_websockets=false
-c model_provider="agent_drive_capture"
```

Each request is also logged to standard error:

```text
capture: <METHOD> <path> <status> <ms>ms <captured | not captured: reason>
```

## What is and is not captured

Captured: HTTP calls to the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs made by an agent that honors the base URL variables, such as `claude` and `codex` in API-key mode.

Each trace file holds:

- The method, the path and the status.
- An allowlist of headers. Request headers: `content-type`, `accept`, `anthropic-version`, `anthropic-beta`, `user-agent`, `x-stainless-lang`, `x-stainless-package-version`, `x-stainless-runtime`. Response headers: `content-type`, `request-id`, `x-request-id`, `x-should-retry`, `retry-after`, the Anthropic and OpenAI rate-limit headers, `openai-processing-ms` and `openai-version`. No `authorization`, `x-api-key`, cookie or other header is saved.
- The request body and the response body. A streaming response is saved as a list of server-sent events. A body that is not valid UTF-8 text is replaced by its length and SHA-256.

Limits and redaction:

- Each body is cut at 4 MiB, and the whole file is kept under 9 MiB. Cut parts are named in the `truncated` list in the file.
- In the saved path, the value of any query parameter whose name contains `key`, `token`, `secret`, `auth` or `signature` is replaced with `[redacted]`. Request URLs are never printed to the terminal with their query string.
- The proxy holds at most 64 MiB of in-flight copies in memory. A request that would exceed that is still forwarded, but it is not captured (`not captured: memory`).
- An upstream connection error returns 502 to the agent and is not captured.

**Prompts are stored.** Everything you send to the model, including any secret you paste into a prompt, is saved in the trace. It is encrypted with your drive key, but it is there. Never put secrets in paths or tags.

Not captured: the Claude desktop app and editor extensions, other traffic from the agent (updates, telemetry), Codex WebSocket transport, Codex ChatGPT-login mode, and agents already pointed at another gateway.

## When capture is disabled

The agent always runs. If capture cannot start, the CLI prints one line and runs COMMAND with its environment and arguments unchanged:

```text
capture disabled: <reason>; running <command> without capture
```

The reasons are:

- A provider is already set. For `claude`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is set. For `codex`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL` is set, or the arguments include a `-c model_provider` or `-c model_providers.*` setting, `--config`, `--profile` or `-p`. For any other command, either variable is set. The message names the flag or variable, never its value.
- Capture could not start: there are no saved API credentials, there is no drive key for the drive, the drive ID is not valid, or the port or the spool directory is not available.

## Spool and upload

Encrypted traces are first written to a local spool at `<config path>.state/capture/<drive id>/`. For the default config path, that is `~/.config/agent-drive/config.json.state/capture/<drive id>/`. The directory has mode `0700` and the files have mode `0600`. A trace is stored as ciphertext plus a small JSON sidecar. Plaintext is never written to disk.

A background task uploads the spool with create-only writes. Behavior:

- **Offline, 5xx or 429:** the traces stay in the spool and are retried on a later run.
- **Stop conditions (401, 402, 403, 413 and other client errors, such as an invalid key, no permission or no quota):** uploads stop and the traces stay for the next run. The CLI prints `capture: uploads stopped (<cause>); traces stay in <spool dir> for the next run`.
- **Server rejects a trace as invalid (400 `validation_error`):** the trace moves to `invalid/` inside the spool directory.
- **Already uploaded (409 exists):** treated as done.
- **Spool full:** the spool holds at most about 512 MiB. The cap is approximate when several capture processes share a spool. Past it, new traces are not saved and are counted as `spool full`.

When COMMAND exits, the CLI waits up to 5 seconds for captures in progress and up to 10 seconds in total for uploads, then prints one summary line:

```text
capture: <uploaded> uploaded, <queued> queued (<MiB> MiB in <spool dir>), <dropped> not captured (<reasons>), <invalid> invalid
```

Traces still queued are uploaded the next time you run `capture` for that drive.

## OpenRouter webhook

OpenRouter can send each trace to your drive. The service receives it over TLS, encrypts it to the drive's trace inbox, and stores it. This works without the CLI. It is not the same as `capture`: the service sees the trace in plaintext for the length of one request.

### Set up in the console

1. Open the drive in the console and choose the traces action (the "Capture traces" dialog).
2. Under "OpenRouter webhook", choose "Add webhook". The console needs the drive key in the tab. If the drive has none loaded, it asks for the recovery file. It checks that the key belongs to this drive before it continues. For a drive with no files, a pasted key cannot be checked, so load the recovery file or a credentials bundle instead.
3. The console creates the drive's trace inbox if the drive has none. It makes the inbox key pair in the browser and stores the private key wrapped under your drive key.
4. The console creates a webhook token. It starts with `adw_` and is shown once. Copy the webhook URL and the headers JSON now:

   ```text
   Webhook URL: https://<origin>/api/webhooks/openrouter/<drive id>
   Headers: {"Authorization":"Bearer adw_<64 hex characters>"}
   ```

5. In OpenRouter, add a Webhook destination with that URL and header. Leave Privacy Mode off for this destination. With it on, traces contain no prompts or replies.

A drive has one active webhook token. "Replace" creates a new token and revokes the old one. "Revoke webhook" stops it. The service stores only the SHA-256 of the token, so a lost token cannot be shown again. Replace it.

### What the endpoint does

`POST /api/webhooks/openrouter/:driveId` with `Authorization: Bearer adw_...`. The body is OTLP JSON, at most 4 MiB. HTTPS is required in production. The token is checked first, before the body is read.

| Case                                         | Response                                             |
| -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| Missing, wrong, revoked or other-drive token | 401                                                  |
| Not HTTPS in production                      | 403                                                  |
| Body over 4 MiB                              | 413 `validation_error`                               |
| `X-Test-Connection` header present           | 200 `{ "ok": true }`. Nothing is stored or charged.  |
| Body is not a JSON object, or has no spans   | 200 `{ "ok": true, "stored": 0 }`                    |
| Stored                                       | 201 `{ "ok": true, "stored": 1, "path": "..." }`     |
| Same body delivered again                    | 200 `{ "ok": true, "stored": 0, "duplicate": true }` |
| The drive has no trace inbox                 | 409 `conflict`                                       |
| Drive quota exceeded                         | 413 `quota_exceeded`                                 |
| Plan budget exceeded                         | 402                                                  |

The path depends only on the body: the earliest span start, the model (`gen_ai.request.model` of the first span) and a SHA-256 prefix. A retry of the same body maps to the same path, which is how duplicates are detected. The stored file is JSON with `v`, `agent` (`openrouter`), `provider`, `receivedAt` and the original `otlp` payload.

To check the connection from a terminal:

```sh
curl -sS -X POST "https://<origin>/api/webhooks/openrouter/<drive id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your webhook token>" \
  -H "X-Test-Connection: 1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

A working token returns `{"ok":true}`.

### Encryption of webhook traces

The service holds the OpenRouter payload in plaintext, in memory, for the length of the request. It seals the payload with a random file key and wraps that key to the drive's trace inbox public key. It does not hold the drive key, it logs nothing from the body or the token, and it cannot read the stored file afterwards. Formats: [Encryption format](crypto.md).

### Read webhook traces

You open them with the same drive key as any other file. The client fetches the drive's inbox record and unwraps the inbox private key locally.

```sh
agent-drive ls --drive <drive id> --prefix /traces/openrouter/
agent-drive get "/traces/openrouter/<date>/<file>.json" --drive <drive id> --output ./trace.json
```

Use `--output` for traces. Without it, `get` prints only small text files, and the limit is 1 MiB. In the MCP server, `get` returns at most 64 KiB inline, and traces are often larger, so use the `download` tool with `outputPath`. See [MCP server and tools](mcp-tools.md).

## Archive old trace files

The `agent-drive-trace-archive` skill moves an agent's old local trace and log files into the drive. It uploads each file, downloads it again, compares SHA-256 hashes, and deletes the local file only when the hashes match. It is meant to run weekly from a scheduler.

Use a dedicated drive and a key with only the `read` and `write` scopes. The script `archive-traces.sh` uploads files older than 7 days (change it with `--older-than-days`) to `/traces/<week>/<path relative to the trace directory>` with the tags `trace` and the week. It skips files modified in the last hour. Run it with `--dry-run` first. A rerun is safe. A failed verification keeps the local file and exits 1.

The skill's full procedure, options and exit codes are in [Agent skills](skills.md).

# CLI reference

This page lists every `agent-drive` command with its flags, environment variables, output and exit behavior. Use it when you need the exact syntax. For task-based walkthroughs, see [Files, versions and sync](files-and-sync.md) and [Share links](sharing.md). The MCP server is documented in [MCP server and tools](mcp-tools.md).

## Install and configuration

Install the CLI (Node 24 or newer):

```sh
npm install -g @dennisonbertram/agent-drive
agent-drive --help
```

Run it without installing by putting `npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest` in front of any command:

```sh
npx -y @dennisonbertram/agent-drive@latest whoami
```

The default API URL is `https://agentdrive.xyz/api`. Override it with `--api` on `login`, or with `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL`.

### Config file

The CLI keeps the API key and drive keys in `~/.config/agent-drive/config.json`, or in the file named by `AGENT_DRIVE_CONFIG`.

- The directory has mode `0700` and the file has mode `0600`. Updates are atomic (write to a temp file, then rename).
- Private state for `sync`, `backup` and `capture` is stored in `<config path>.state`. An existing state directory with unsafe permissions is rejected without changing its mode.
- Config updates take an exclusive lock, the directory `<config path>.lock`. If a CLI process crashes it may leave the lock behind. Remove it manually only after you confirm no Agent Drive process is running. A command that waits more than 10 seconds for the lock fails with a message naming the stale lock.
- Drive keys never leave your machine. They are not sent to the API or to storage.

### Environment variables

| Variable                     | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_CONFIG`         | Path of the config file.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_API_URL`        | API URL. Overrides the saved value.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_API_KEY`        | API key. Overrides the saved value. `login` saves it instead of starting browser approval.                                                                                                           |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_MACHINE`        | Machine name sent with each request. Defaults to the host name. Also used in the default `backup` prefix.                                                                                            |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_CREDENTIALS`    | A credentials bundle (`adcred1.…`). Merged in memory at startup and never written to disk. Its drives count as backed up. The saved config and the explicit variables above take precedence over it. |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>` | Drive key for one drive. The drive ID is uppercased and every non-alphanumeric character becomes `_`.                                                                                                |
| `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY`            | Drive key used for any drive.                                                                                                                                                                        |

### Drive key precedence

The CLI looks for a drive key in this order:

1. `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY_<DRIVE_ID>`
2. `AGENT_DRIVE_KEY`
3. The file named by `--key-file PATH`
4. The key saved in the config file for the current API origin

### The `--drive` default

Every command that works on a drive takes `--drive ID`. If you leave it out, the CLI uses the only drive key saved for the current API origin. With none or several, it exits with code 1 and lists the configured IDs. `backup` and `check` follow the same rule; `check` picks the only usable drive.
